For the financial year ended 31 July 2026, revenue increased by 17.7%, from $73.0 
million to $85.9 million. Revenue comprised $15.7 million from the sale of goods, 
representing 18.3% of total revenue, and $70.2 million from the rendering of services, 
representing 81.7%. 
 
(Source: company annual report)  
 
However, profit attributable to owners of the company was only $1.416 million, while the 
group's 48% share of the profit contribution from KESM Industries Berhad1 amounted to 
approximately $1.419 million. The rendering of services through KESM was therefore the 
principal contributor to the group's attributable earnings. The group's core operations 
outside of testing services achieved break-even, at best. 
 
Revenue from the sale of goods has declined substantially over the longer term, although 
FY2026 recorded a rebound: 
 
- 
FY2020: $37.2 million  
- 
FY2021: $40.6 million  
- 
FY2022: $25.1 million  
- 
FY2023: $19.3 million 
- 
FY2024: $12.3 million  
- 
FY2025: $9.2 million  
- 
FY2026: $15.7 million 
 
(i) 
Can management explain the underlying drivers of this longer-term decline 
and the latest recovery? What evidence, if any, gives management 
confidence that the FY2026 rebound in sale of goods represents a 
sustainable recovery rather than a temporary increase in customer orders? 
 
 
1 The group's 48% interest in KESM Industries Berhad contributed approximately $1.419 million to profit 
attributable to shareholders, based on the $1.537 million profit attributable to the 52% non-controlling 
interest (Note 12(b) Investment in subsidiaries; page 113). 

In his statement to shareholders, the chairman highlighted that the group’s burn-in and 
testing capabilities are growing alongside market opportunities, particularly in AI-related 
power modules, power devices and automotive applications.  
 
(ii) 
What proportion of FY2026 revenue was attributable specifically to AI-
related power module testing? How does management estimate the 
addressable market for these services? Given the substantial investment in 
AI infrastructure over recent years, why has the group not captured a 
greater share of the resulting demand, and what specific capabilities or 
customer relationships are needed to do so?

The attendance of directors at board and board committee meetings is shown on page 
60 of the annual report and reproduced below. 
 
(Source: company annual report; emphasis added)  
 
Ms Sandy Foo Fei Ying was absent from two of the three board meetings in FY2026. The 
director also did not attend the two audit and risk committee meetings, and missed one 
meeting each of the nominating committee and remuneration committee. 
 
The company attributed the director’s absences to “unavoidable professional commitments 
and unforeseen travel disruption”.  
 
(i) 
Can the company provide further details of the circumstances that resulted 
in the director missing these meetings? For the meetings missed due to 
unavoidable professional commitments, had the director previously 

confirmed her availability before subsequently withdrawing given that 
board and board committee meetings are planned months ahead? 
 
(ii) 
Can the company confirm that the director did not participate remotely 
through voice calls or video conferencing even though it is allowed in the 
company’s constitution? 
 
(Source: company annual report; emphasis added)  
 
Since the director’s appointment in February 2021, the director has had recurring absences 
from board and board committee meetings.  

(iii) 
Given that the director is seeking re-election, how did the nominating 
committee assess whether she has sufficient time and capacity to discharge 
her responsibilities as a director and committee member? What specific 
evidence supports the committee's recommendation that she remains 
suitable for re-election? In addition, given that the director did not attend 
any of the audit and risk committee meetings during FY2026, how did the 
board satisfy itself that the director had effectively discharged her 
responsibilities as a committee member? 
 
The director is also a practising lawyer with significant professional responsibilities2.  
 
(iv) 
How has the nominating committee assessed the demands of the director’s 
external professional commitments against the time required to discharge 
the director’s responsibilities to the group, considering the director’s past 
attendance trend? 
 
(v) 
How can the company secretary and the company work together with the 
board to improve the attendance of directors at board meetings?

On 16 January 2026, SGX RegCo issued a Regulator’s Column on forward guidance, in 
which the regulator strongly encouraged issuers to provide meaningful forward-looking 
disclosures. 
 
SGX RegCo noted that forward-looking information consistently ranks highly among the 
information sought by investors, including institutional investors and research analysts, 
particularly regarding anticipated earnings and management’s strategy for achieving those 
outcomes. The regulator also clarified that forward guidance does not require auditor sign-
off and that issuers are not expected to update guidance immediately for every change in 
circumstances. Issuers should nevertheless make timely announcements in accordance with 
existing listing rules relating to material information and price-sensitive developments. 
 
SGX RegCo also highlighted that forward guidance should be viewed as a means for 
companies to signal confidence, build credibility with investors, and potentially support 
long-term shareholder value, rather than as a compliance exercise. 
 
The Regulator’s Column can be accessed here: 
https://www.sgxgroup.com/media-centre/20260116-regulators-column-forward-
guidance-why-it-matters-and-how-get-it 
 
 
2 In a 27 March 2025 article published by The Business Times, a Sandy Foo, identified as deputy head of the 
corporate and transactional group and head of mergers and acquisitions at Rajah & Tann, was reported to be 
handling "a handful" of privatisation transactions involving SGX Mainboard-listed companies, with deal 
values of up to several billion dollars. (See https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-
markets/indonesias-widjaja-family-moves-delist-sinarmas-land-sgx-more-large-cap-exits-horizon) 

(i) 
Given SGX RegCo’s encouragement of forward guidance and its view that 
such disclosures can enhance investor confidence and credibility, has the 
board considered providing forward guidance for FY26/27 on the group’s 
performance, outlook, key operating assumptions, and strategic priorities? 
If not, why not?
